new.title: Walk the walls of Gaziantep Castle
new.desc: The citadel stands on a mound in the old town and began as a Roman-era watchtower. Its walls were rebuilt in the Seljuk and Ottoman periods, with restoration finished in 1481. The February 2023 quakes damaged it; restoration of its bastions and ramparts ended in late 2025.
new.tip: Reports from December 2025 say the restored castle was handed over and due to reopen within days. Check current opening before going, as no firm reopening date was found.
new.q: Gaziantep Kalesi, Kale Mahallesi, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: See the Gypsy Girl at the Zeugma Mosaic Museum
new.desc: The museum holds Roman mosaics rescued from Zeugma on the Euphrates before the Birecik dam flooded the site. It opened in 2011 and shows over 1,700 square metres of floors, with the Gypsy Girl as the best-known piece. It reopened in April 2023 after a precautionary closure and was not structurally damaged.
new.tip: Allow two hours. Go early to avoid tour groups, and check whether the Turkey Museum Pass is accepted.
new.q: Zeugma Mozaik Müzesi, Şehitkamil, Gaziantep

new.title: Trace Hittite to Byzantine times at the Archaeology Museum
new.desc: The Gaziantep Museum of Archaeology holds finds from the Neolithic to the Byzantine era, with Hittite, Assyrian, Hellenistic and Roman coin collections. The building was damaged in the 2023 earthquake and reopened after reinforcement, repair and a new roof.
new.tip: About a 15-minute walk from the castle. Confirm hours on the day, since the reopening is recent.
new.q: Gaziantep Arkeoloji Müzesi, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Relive the 1920 siege at the Panorama Museum
new.desc: The Gaziantep Defence and Heroism Panorama Museum sits beside the castle and uses dioramas to tell the city's resistance to the French in 1920-21. Statues of local heroes stand at the entrance.
new.tip: Visitors say it suits those interested in the war; combine it with the castle walk.
new.q: Gaziantep Savunması Panorama Müzesi, Kale Mahallesi, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Learn the city's kitchen at the Emine Göğüş Culinary Museum
new.desc: A stone house of 1904 restored by the metropolitan municipality, it explains Gaziantep's food culture with kitchen displays and demonstrations. Its restoration was completed after the 2023 quakes. Gaziantep is a UNESCO Creative City of Gastronomy.
new.tip: Visit before a food tour to see the regional dishes explained.
new.q: Emine Göğüş Mutfak Müzesi, Bey Mahallesi, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Tour the Hamam Museum opposite the castle
new.desc: A historic Antep bath restored by the metropolitan municipality and opened as a museum in 2015. Two large former bath rooms show the city's hamam culture.
new.tip: Small museum, about 30 minutes. The entrance fee is modest; confirm the current price.
new.q: Gaziantep Hamam Müzesi, Kale Mahallesi, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Visit the Mevlevi lodge museum at Tekke Camii
new.desc: The Mevlevi Culture and Foundation Works Museum opened in 2007 in a dervish lodge dating to 1638, in the courtyard of the Tekke Mosque.
new.tip: Quiet courtyard, pleasant in the afternoon heat. Dress modestly.
new.q: Mevlevihane Vakıf Müzesi, Tepebaşı Mahallesi, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Browse the Gaziantep City Museum in Bayazhan
new.desc: Bayazhan is a courtyard building of 1909 on Atatürk Boulevard. It houses the city museum with interactive displays on local history, plus a courtyard restaurant.
new.tip: Combine with the Kendirli church area. Check opening hours at the door.
new.q: Bayazhan Gaziantep Kent Müzesi, Atatürk Bulvarı, Bey Mahallesi, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Peek at 600 handmade toys in the Toy Museum
new.desc: The Gaziantep Game and Toy Museum shows about 600 handmade toys in a restored house in the city centre.
new.tip: Good with children; a short visit.
new.q: Gaziantep Oyun ve Oyuncak Müzesi, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: See the Nakıpoğlu House war museum
new.desc: The Gaziantep War Museum occupies the Nakıpoğlu House and commemorates the 6,317 people who died defending the city in 1920-21.
new.tip: Better value if combined with the Panorama Museum.
new.q: Gaziantep Savaş Müzesi, Nakıpoğlu Konağı, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Look for the walnut minbar at Boyacı Mosque
new.desc: One of the city's oldest buildings, begun by Kadı Kemalettin in 1211 and finished in 1357. It is known for a very old wooden minbar on wheels.
new.tip: Remove shoes and dress modestly; avoid prayer times.
new.q: Boyacı Camii, Boyacı Mahallesi, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Enter the Liberation Mosque, once St Mary's Church
new.desc: This large Armenian cathedral of the Holy Mother of God was converted to a mosque after the French occupation of 1918-21 and is now the Kurtuluş (Liberation) Mosque in Tepebaşı.
new.tip: Admire the stonework from outside; enter only outside prayer times.
new.q: Kurtuluş Camii, Tepebaşı Mahallesi, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: See Şirvani Mosque, restored after the 2023 quake
new.desc: Also called İki Şerefeli Cami, it is among the city's oldest mosques, built by Şirvani Mehmet Efendi. The earthquake damaged it and the Ministry reopened it after restoration.
new.tip: Look at the restored minarets and dome from the street.
new.q: Şirvani Camii, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Visit the Ali İhsan Göğüş Museum in the old Bey quarter
new.desc: A museum and Gaziantep research centre in the old Bey quarter, listed as open daily and free of charge. It sits a few minutes' walk from the Atatürk Boulevard end of the old town.
new.tip: Pair it with the nearby Emine Göğüş Culinary Museum; allow about 30 minutes.
new.q: Ali İhsan Göğüş Müzesi, Ali Özalgan Sokak, Bey Mahallesi, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Duck into the vaulted Zincirli Bedesten
new.desc: Built in 1781 by Hüseyin Pasha of Darende, this covered market once sold meat, fruit and vegetables wholesale and now has about 70 shops with kutnu silk, copper and souvenirs. The Ministry reopened it after restoration.
new.tip: Look for silk scarves and kutnu textiles.
new.q: Zincirli Bedesten, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Wander the courtyard of Anadolu Han
new.desc: A two-storey caravanserai from the early 19th century, repaired in 1985, with a central courtyard in the bazaar quarter.
new.tip: Fits a half-hour; open during bazaar hours.
new.q: Anadolu Hanı, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Admire Şeyh Fethullah Mosque, built 1563
new.desc: The mosque was built in 1563 with a hamam and a medrese beside it. It was badly damaged in the 2023 earthquakes and reopened for worship after restoration.
new.tip: Respect prayer times and wear modest clothing.
new.q: Şeyh Fethullah Camii, Şehreküstü, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: See Ömeriye Mosque, linked to Caliph Omar
new.desc: Tradition says the first building here was connected to Caliph Omar; the present mosque was restored in 1850.
new.tip: Modest dress needed.
new.q: Ömeriye Camii, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Eat ali nazik kebab at İmam Çağdaş
new.desc: A kebab and baklava house on the Uzun Çarşı that has served since 1887, known for ali nazik (kebab on smoked aubergine puree and yogurt) and lahmacun. The baklava counter is at the front.
new.tip: Try ali nazik, then a plate of yaş baklava. Expect a queue at lunch.
new.q: İmam Çağdaş, Uzun Çarşı, Şekeroğlu Mahallesi, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Start the day with beyran at Metanet
new.desc: Metanet Lokantası serves beyran, a fiery lamb and rice breakfast soup, from early morning until it sells out. It draws a local crowd by 7.
new.tip: Ask for beyran with or without spice; arrive before 9.
new.q: Metanet Lokantası, Kozluca Caddesi, Kozluca Mahallesi, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Order katmer at Katmerci Zekeriya Usta
new.desc: A katmer specialist in Çukur Mahallesi, where thin dough is filled with clotted cream (kaymak) and pistachio and baked. Fodor's lists it as a top katmer spot.
new.tip: Eat it fresh for breakfast; it is rich, so share one.
new.q: Katmerci Zekeriya Usta, Çukur Mahallesi, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Buy pistachio baklava at Güllüoğlu in Elmacı Pazarı
new.desc: The family says its Elmacı Pazarı shop opened in 1871; it makes classic baklava, dolama, sobiyet and bülbül yuvası. Fodor's calls it a small shop widely seen as among the country's best.
new.tip: Buy a box of mixed baklava and eat a piece fresh.
new.q: Güllüoğlu Baklava, Elmacı Pazarı, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Order şöbiyet at Zeki İnal
new.desc: Baklava maker Zeki İnal is known for şöbiyet baked in a stone oven heated by pipes.
new.tip: Go around 9am or order a day ahead.
new.q: Baklavacı Zeki İnal, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Sip menengiç coffee in Tahmis Kahvesi
new.desc: Said to be the city's oldest coffeehouse, founded in the 17th century near Elmacı Pazarı. It serves menengiç coffee made from terebinth berries, zahter tea and baklava.
new.tip: Order menengiç and a baklava plate.
new.q: Tahmis Kahvesi, Elmacı Pazarı, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Try kuşleme and simit kebab at Halil Usta
new.desc: Kebapçı Halil Usta is known for kuşleme (lamb tenderloin kebab) and simit kebab, with a well-liked salad.
new.tip: Lunch only; closes mid-afternoon.
new.q: Kebapçı Halil Usta, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Eat grilled liver at Löküs Ciğer
new.desc: Löküs is known for ciğer (liver) cooked by constantly turning it over the fire, a Gaziantep morning and lunch dish.
new.tip: Order liver kebab with flatbread and onions.
new.q: Löküs Ciğer, Gaziantep

new.title: Taste alaca soup and saray kebabı at Aşina
new.desc: Aşina serves Gaziantep home cooking such as alaca çorbası, saray kebabı and yuvarlama.
new.tip: Try yuvarlama or a set of home dishes.
new.q: Aşina Restoran, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Eat thin lahmacun at Üçler
new.desc: Üçler Kebap Lahmacun is praised for thin, isot-spiked lahmacun, which locals roll with parsley.
new.tip: Order several; they are small.
new.q: Üçler Kebap Lahmacun, Gaziantep

new.title: Dine in Mustafa Paşa Han at Hışvahan
new.desc: Hışvahan is a restaurant in the restored Mustafa Paşa Han near the old bazaar, serving şiveydiz soup, soğan kebabı, sour-cherry kısır and cennet çamuru dessert.
new.tip: Try the soup and dessert in the courtyard.
new.q: Hışva Han, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Order kavurma at Muhsinzade in the coppersmith bazaar
new.desc: Muhsinzade Türk İşi Kebap is in the Bakırcılar Çarşısı and serves kavurma, nohut dürüm and, on Fridays, firik pilavı.
new.tip: Lunch spot inside the bazaar.
new.q: Muhsinzade Türk Şiş Kebap, Külekçi Çarşısı Sokak, Boyacı, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Bite into nohut dürüm at Dürümcü Recep Usta
new.desc: Dürümcü Recep Usta in Karşıyaka is listed for nohut dürüm, a wrap filled with chickpeas and grilled meat.
new.tip: Quick lunch; usually busy.
new.q: Dürümcü Recep Usta, Şehit Mehmet Sait Elçi Sokağı, Değirmiçem, Şehitkamil, Gaziantep

new.title: Eat çiğ köfte under the castle at Kasap Yaşar Usta
new.desc: Kasap Yaşar Usta sits near the castle with outdoor seating under trees and serves tavuk şiş and raw-meat çiğ köfte.
new.tip: Evening outdoor meal.
new.q: Kasap Yaşar Usta, Kale Mahallesi, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Watch coppersmiths in the Bakırcılar Çarşısı
new.desc: The coppersmiths' bazaar has traded for over 500 years; workshops hammer copper pots and trays on the spot, with leather, olive-oil soap and spices alongside.
new.tip: Shops are relaxed; bargain politely.
new.q: Bakırcılar Çarşısı, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Buy handmade yemeni shoes near Zincirli
new.desc: Yemeni shoes are hand-stitched leather loafers sold on the street between the coppersmith bazaar and Zincirli Bedesten.
new.tip: Prices were about 200 lira a pair on a recent visit.
new.q: Yemenici Hayri Usta, Gaziantep

new.title: Walk the old Bey quarter from Kendirli to the castle
new.desc: Narrow streets of restored stone houses lie around the castle and Kendirli church; the Şahinbey alleys are best in late afternoon light.
new.tip: Allow two hours and go late afternoon.
new.q: Bey Mahallesi, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Spend a day at Gaziantep Zoo and Natural Life Park
new.desc: Turkey's largest zoo in Burç Forest opened in 2001, with about 4,000 animals, a safari park (2018) and a large aquarium.
new.tip: Take a full day and go in spring or autumn.
new.q: Gaziantep Doğal Yaşam Parkı, Çamtepe, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Stroll Gaziantep Botanical Garden
new.desc: Established in 2009 as an education centre, it holds about 750 plant species and over 30,000 plants.
new.tip: Spring is best.
new.q: Gaziantep Botanik Bahçesi, Zübeyde Hanım Bulvarı, Gazi Mahallesi, Şehitkamil, Gaziantep

new.title: Eat and learn at the Mutfak Sanatları Merkezi
new.desc: The municipal culinary arts centre trains cooks and serves a weekly-changing regional menu including yuvarlama and içli köfte.
new.tip: Call ahead about courses.
new.q: Mutfak Sanatları Merkezi, Karagöz Mahallesi, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Shop for pistachios and isot in Elmacı Pazarı
new.desc: The spice bazaar sells pistachios, isot pepper, pomegranate molasses and pepper paste to take home.
new.tip: Buy vacuum-packed to carry home.
new.q: Elmacı Pazarı, Karatarla Mahallesi, Şahinbey, Gaziantep

new.title: Take in the city from the Kanalıcı Mosque park
new.desc: An uphill mosque with a large flag and a park with views over the old city.
new.tip: Go at sunset.
new.q: Kanalıcı Camii, Şahinbey, Gaziantep
